newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares drift lower, outlook range-bound.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares drift lower, outlook range-bound.

text.p: Share prices finished broadly lower at the Bombay and National exchanges on Tuesday dragged down by institutional selling, brokers said.
They said the market lacked follow-up support after last week's upsurge sparked by easier liquidity and cuts in lending rates by banks.
"The market's is directionless," said trader Ramnik Parikh. "People are selling at small rallies."
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index dropped 27.18 points, or 0.83 percent, to a provisional 3,237.34.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index lost 6.97 points, or 0.74 percent, to close at a provisional 929.03.
The 500-share CRISIL index shed 5.49 points, or 0.88 percent, to a provisional 619.24.
Hindustan Lever, ACC, Gujarat Ambuja Cement, L&T, Reliance, and ITC were some of the stocks sold by the institutions, traders said.
State-run insurance firms were the only major buyers but their orders were in tiny lots, they said.
Sandoz fell 46 rupees to a provisional 261, hit by an unfavourable stocks swap merger ratio with Hindustan Ciba-Geigy.
Sandoz said on Monday it will offer its shareholders 10 shares in Hindustan Ciba-Geigy in exchange for every 17 shares they hold in Sandoz India.
Hindustan Ciba-Geigy rose 416.25 rupees to a provisional 2,771.25.
ACC fell 30 rupees to 1,525, TELCO 10.25 to 423, Hind Lever 7.25 to 803.75, L&T 3.75 to 229.50 and M&M 10.50 to 315.
SBI gained 3.0 rupees to 234.50, ITC 5.75 to 321.25 and BSES 2.50 to 193.25.
